decompositions.boundaries: Change 1 (A to B): replace the comma-separated export by JSON Lines; hands over a valid state where both formats are available and the outside consumer can adopt JSON Lines. Boundary 1/2: the outside consumer has adopted and reads JSON Lines (adoption must happen before the next step can start). Change 2: retire the comma-separated reader once that consumer reads JSON Lines; hands over a state where only JSON Lines is used but the transition option still exists. Boundary 2/3: the reader is retired, so nothing depends on the dual-serving option. Change 3: remove the transition option that served both, retiring what Change 1 introduced.

explanation.current: A: the notes tool exports a header row id,title,body then one comma-separated line per note (H1), writes every note without dropping any (H2), and for an empty store exits with 0 and writes only the header (H3). All three Cases are green today; this is evidence of A only.
explanation.intended: B: export writes one JSON object per line and no header (B1), still writes every note with none dropped (B2), and for an empty store exits with 0 and writes nothing (B3). B1 and the empty-output part of B3 are new and need Cases of their own.
explanation.changes: The comma-separated format and header row are replaced by JSON Lines (B1 introduced). The no-note-dropped guarantee and the exit code 0 on an empty store are kept. One Change suffices for this transition: one boundary, one baseline, one target.
explanation.superseded_and_protected: Superseded (historical): H1 (header row plus comma-separated lines) and the writes-only-the-header part of H3; these Cases are recorded as superseded and must not be kept green as protections of B. Protected (enduring): H2/B2 (every note written, none dropped) and the exit code 0 on an empty store from H3/B3; these Cases stay and are re-run against B. H3 is mixed and is split by kind.
explanation.evidence: B's own green Cases show only that B holds, and A's green Cases show only that A held. Transition evidence, kept in the Change record, is needed: the same store run through both exports gives the same set of notes (enduring part kept), the header Case is recorded as superseded, and the enduring Cases (no note dropped, exit 0 on empty store) are re-run green against B.

observerVerdict.boundaryReasoning: This is the strongest on the boundaries. Each Change says what state it hands over, each boundary says why order matters (adoption before retirement, nothing depends on the dual option before removal), and no Change is planned in detail. D1 is justified as one baseline and one target.
